input.zip_bytes: truncated mid-entry; central directory records an entry the local file data does not fully contain

expected.error_category: corrupt archive: central directory / local file mismatch

notes: D-006 correction, not oracle parity. MSC 1's own pre-flight check, validateZipArchive (lines 253-274), already refuses to proceed on a bad archive -- but it does so by shelling out to '/usr/bin/unzip -t' (line 262) and trusting its exit status, a black box whose exact validation depth (checksum-only vs. full structural cross-check) is whatever that specific unzip build implements and isn't specified anywhere MSC 2 can pin against. Phase 6 replaces this with a real Rust zip-reading crate that parses the central directory and cross-checks it against local file headers directly, so the validation logic is auditable and consistent across all three platforms rather than depending on each OS's bundled unzip binary. The *behavior* being preserved (reject corrupt archives before touching any live world data) is baseline; the *mechanism* is the correction.
